title: Resolve egress-resolver starvation during dedicated-node scale-down causing tenant DNS blackout
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalation: multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent DNS failures (NXDOMAIN / timeouts) for internal hostnames after rapid GPU pool scale-down events. Root cause traced to resolver agent starvation on dedicated egress nodes: when many tenants are drained simultaneously, the per-tenant resolver worker queue can be starved by aggressive connection rebind/cleanup, causing resolver probes to be delayed and ephemeral SNAT mappings to expire. The result is a 30-90s window where tenant resolver state is inconsistent and DNS responses are lost or answered via default external resolver, exposing internal hostnames. This ticket captures the investigation, mitigation, and the targeted production fix to ensure tenant isolation and stable resolver affinity during scale events.
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha Patel: Triage call with SRE and SEs after PagerDuty escalation. Reproduced on staging by simulating 120 concurrent tenant drains with bursty egress flows. Noted correlation with dedicated pool autoscaler shrinking by >30% in <45s.

2026-02-26 Marco Rivera: Instrumented resolver-agent with per-tenant queue histograms and added tracing for SNAT allocation/expiry. Found long tail of 60-120s delays in resolver probe scheduling when worker threads hit 100% CPU during cleanup.

2026-03-01 Marco Rivera: Short-term mitigation rolled: throttle concurrent tenant drains for Dedicated clusters (control-plane flag) and increase resolver-agent probe retry backoff. Applied to two affected regions; customer reported improvement. Added postmortem stub in Confluence.

2026-03-03 Priya Desai (SRE): Observability changes merged — dashboard panels for resolver queue depth and per-tenant SNAT reuse rate. Alert rule created (RESOLVER-QUEUED-50) to trigger when >50 tenants have queue depth > 5 for >1m.

2026-03-06 Marco Rivera: Proposed permanent fix PR: 1) make resolver-agent use priority queue for egress tasks (favor active tenant bindings), 2) extend ephemeral SNAT lease during scale events, 3) add non-blocking defer on host teardown to allow pending resolver probes to finish. Opened RFC and benchmarked on staging with synthetic workloads.

2026-03-09 Design Review: Trade-offs discussed — extending SNAT leases reduces port pressure but increases ephemeral port utilization. Decided to combine SNAT lease extension with tighter drain throttling and a lightweight retry-probe rather than aggressive rebinds. Need SRE sign-off for autoscaler throttle default.

2026-03-11 Marco Rivera: Fixed edge-case where resolver backoff could starve low-priority tenants indefinitely; added fairness window. PR #4628 under code review. Unit tests + integration test harness added for staged scale-down scenario.

2026-03-12 Customer update: SE sent interim report to affected customers; migration guide with recommended autoscaler settings attached. Preparing canary rollout for runtime-2.4 with feature flag to allow fast rollback.

Next steps: finish code review, run canary on two Dedicated clusters with heavy multi-tenant drains, monitor RESOLVER-QUEUED-50 and customer tickets, and schedule post-deploy follow-up with CS and affected customers.
